segments.text: A few years ago, I passed on an opportunity that  Istill think about sometimes. It was a small investment a friend mentioned, nothing too risky, just something new he'd been looking into. He was really into it, talking about how it had potential, how it was worth getting in early. I remember nodding along, half-listening and saying something like, "Yeah, maybe I'll check it out later," but I never did.
I got busy, forgot about it, and moved on with other things.

A few months later, he brought it up again, this time with a big smile. He said it actually worked out. He'd made a pretty decent return, and I was genuinely happy for him. But in the back of my mind, I had that little voice going, "Man, you could've done that, too." It wasn't even about the money. It was more about the hesitation, that small pause that turned into inaction. I had the information, the time, and the chance. I just didn't act. I think about that sometimes, not with regret, just with curiosity. Like, how many moments like that pass by without us even noticing? And the thing is, I've missed other opportunities since then. We all have.
But that one sticks out because it was such an easy yes, I just didn't say it.

I guess that's the thing about decisions. Sometimes, it's not about taking big risks. It's about trusting yourself enough to move when something feels right. Because every time you say, "Maybe later," you're betting that chance will come around again, and sometimes, it doesn't.
